pr.title: Anonymous: Add configurable device limit

raw_findings.body: The generated injector still invokes the old constructor/provider signatures, so the server package fails to compile until Wire output is regenerated and the stale AnonStore provider wiring is reconciled.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Build-time dependency injection code calls functions with obsolete argument lists.
raw_findings.impact: The generated injector still invokes the old constructor/provider signatures, so the server package fails to compile until Wire output is regenerated and the stale AnonStore provider wiring is reconciled.
raw_findings.root_cause: The dependency-injection constructor signature was changed without updating the generated DI artifacts and provider graph.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the Wire provider set to remove or adapt the old AnonStore binding, then regenerate and commit the server Wire injector so it passes db.DB to this constructor and supplies the new AnonDBStore arguments correctly.
raw_findings.title: Update the generated Wire injector for the changed constructor
raw_findings.trigger: Building the server with the committed Wire-generated injector after this constructor changes from accepting an anonstore.AnonStore to accepting db.DB.

raw_findings.body: Both requests can observe the same pre-insert count and each proceed to the later upsert, resulting in more active devices than the configured limit and both anonymous sessions being admitted.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent requests pass a stale capacity check and exceed the configured device limit.
raw_findings.impact: Both requests can observe the same pre-insert count and each proceed to the later upsert, resulting in more active devices than the configured limit and both anonymous sessions being admitted.
raw_findings.root_cause: The capacity check is performed separately from the later insert/upsert and does not reserve a slot.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Perform the count/reservation and insert-or-update in one serialized transaction or use a database-backed lock/admission record so only one new device can claim the remaining capacity at a time.
raw_findings.title: Make device-limit admission atomic
raw_findings.trigger: With a positive limit (for example, 1), two new device IDs authenticate concurrently while the current count is below the limit, including requests handled by separate Grafana instances.

raw_findings.body: The first request returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, but tagDeviceUI has already placed that ID in the local cache before this update returns the error. The retry sees the cache hit, skips the database limit check, and is authenticated despite the configured limit.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A rejected device is treated as recently admitted on subsequent requests, bypassing limit enforcement.
raw_findings.impact: The first request returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, but tagDeviceUI has already placed that ID in the local cache before this update returns the error. The retry sees the cache hit, skips the database limit check, and is authenticated despite the configured limit.
raw_findings.root_cause: The newly introduced limit-rejection path can fail after the caller has marked the device as successfully tagged in the local cache.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Only add the device cache entry after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds, or remove the entry whenever the store call returns an error.
raw_findings.title: Do not cache devices whose limit check rejects them
raw_findings.trigger: After the active-device limit has been reached, a new device ID makes an anonymous request and then retries against the same server within the local-cache TTL.

finding.verifier_reason: The patch shows ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now accepts db.DB and calls ProvideAnonDBStore inline. The wire.go context (L374-375) shows anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore is still registered in the provider set with a binding to AnonStore interface. The claim that Wire output is stale is speculative - the patch itself is self-consistent and the provider set appears updated. No concrete evidence of a build failure introduced by this patch.

finding.title: Do not cache devices whose limit check rejects them
finding.trigger: After the active-device limit has been reached, a new device ID makes an anonymous request and then retries against the same server within the local-cache TTL.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim requires tagDeviceUI to cache the device before CreateOrUpdateDevice is called. However, examining impl.go lines 80-98, the cache is set at line 87 (localCache.SetDefault) BEFORE CreateOrUpdateDevice is called at line 93. If CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache entry already exists. BUT the claim's trigger scenario is flawed: on retry, the cache hit at line 83-84 returns nil early, never calling CreateOrUpdateDevice again - so the device is NOT 'authenticated' via the store, it just returns success from tagDeviceUI. The actual authentication happens in client.go where ErrDeviceLimitReached is checked and returned to deny auth. The cache bypass doesn't grant authentication.
